question: Should RFC 0018 establish required/advisory conditions, activation-scoped plugin provider registration, and explicit `gateway.readiness` selection as OpenClaw's v1 readiness contract?
rationale: Tests and runtime proof can validate the implementation, but they cannot decide whether this configuration and plugin API should become a supported long-term product contract.

options.title: Accept the v1 contract
options.body: Approve the proposed model and proceed with the linked implementation while preserving the documented opt-in and compatibility guarantees.

options.title: Narrow the initial contract
options.body: Accept canonical core conditions first but defer either plugin registration, operator-selected criteria, or the CLI projection to a later RFC.

options.title: Defer readiness extensibility
options.body: Keep the existing fixed evaluator and close or pause this RFC until a stronger maintainer-owned use case warrants new public surface.

recommendation.title: Accept the v1 contract
recommendation.body: Approve the proposed model and proceed with the linked implementation while preserving the documented opt-in and compatibility guarantees.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to recent Gateway architecture and startup behavior around the proposed contract.
